description: Merge scenarios (sync-protocol.md sections 4 and 5). Each case must give the expected state for every delivery order of input.records (plus the emitted records, for cases with an edit).

cases.name: concurrent edits to different fields both survive
cases.note: A renames the bill while B changes the payment; neither edit is lost.

cases.name: same field: later wall time wins regardless of device
cases.note: B's device ID is higher, but A's edit is 5 seconds later.

cases.name: same field, same wall time: higher counter wins
cases.note: The counter is compared before the device ID.

cases.name: same field, same wall time and counter: higher device ID wins
identical HLC with different values: value order breaks the tie
cases.note: Only a buggy writer produces this, but merge must still converge: null < false < true < numbers < strings; numbers by value; strings by UTF-8 bytes.

cases.name: delete wins over an earlier edit
cases.note: The tombstone is an ordinary field; other fields keep merging but the row is not live.

cases.name: an edit after a delete does not bring the row back
cases.note: B edited a row it had not yet seen deleted. Only deleted=false undeletes.

cases.name: undelete: a later deleted=false brings the row back
cases.note: B restored the bill after A deleted it.

cases.name: delete after undelete: the later write wins
cases.note: Three devices toggle the tombstone; the last write wins.

cases.name: duplicate mark-paid on two devices yields one payment
cases.note: Both devices derive the same payment ID from (bill, period), so the payment is counted once.

cases.name: duplicate mark-paid with different amounts: one payment, later amount wins
cases.note: B typed 60 offline, A typed 55 ten seconds later.

cases.name: unmark then remark: the payment is live and counted once
cases.note: A marks and unmarks; B, after syncing, marks it again.

cases.name: unmark concurrent with an amount edit: stays unmarked
cases.note: Editing the amount does not re-mark the payment.

cases.name: rows whose create has not arrived are pending, not live
cases.note: A row is live only when its deleted field is present and false. Edits are kept until the create arrives.

cases.name: out-of-order delivery of a create and three later edits converges
cases.note: Every delivery order gives the same result; nothing is applied 'in arrival order'.

cases.name: duplicate delivery is harmless
cases.note: Re-reading a file applies the same records again; the state does not change.

cases.name: a checkpoint set after an offline payment absorbs it
cases.note: B paid 100 offline (HLC +100s). A, not having seen it, typed a statement balance of 950 (HLC +200s). The checkpoint is later, so the payment is treated as already reflected in 950.

cases.name: a payment after the checkpoint is subtracted
cases.note: A sets 950; B pays 100 later (by HLC).

cases.name: HLC, not paidAt, decides whether a payment is after the checkpoint
cases.note: B's wall clock said 11:00 (before the checkpoint), but its HLC is later, so the payment counts.

cases.name: unmark after a statement balance raises Remaining back
cases.note: Remaining 1000, mark paid 100 (900), statement balance 880 typed (checkpoint absorbs the payment), unmark. The payment is at or before the checkpoint, so unmark also raises the checkpoint by its amount: 880 + 100 = 980.

cases.name: remark after that unmark subtracts once
cases.note: The re-mark is after the new checkpoint (+300s), so it subtracts: 980 - 100 = 880. Before this rule the result was 780 (subtracted twice).

cases.name: markPaid on a payment already live writes only amountPaid and paidAt
cases.note: Writing deleted=false again would move the mark HLC past the checkpoint and subtract a payment the checkpoint already includes. The payment stays absorbed, so the amount change does not move Remaining.

cases.name: markPaid on a live payment after the checkpoint changes the amount it subtracts
cases.note: The payment is after the checkpoint, so its new amount counts: 1000 - 120.

cases.name: unmarking a migrated payment raises Remaining back
cases.note: Migration stamps the checkpoint and the payment with one HLC, so the payment is absorbed (equal HLC). Unmark gives it back: 1145 + 55.

cases.name: unmark while Remaining is clamped at zero uses the unclamped value
cases.note: Checkpoint 50 absorbs the 30 payment; a later 60 payment shows Remaining 0 (unclamped -10). Unmarking the 30 gives -10 + 30 = 20, not 0 + 30.

cases.name: deleting an extra payment absorbed by a checkpoint raises Remaining back
cases.note: Same rule for Extra payments.

cases.name: unmarking a set-aside never writes a checkpoint
cases.note: Set-asides never count against Remaining, so there is nothing to give back.

cases.name: known limitation: a device that missed the mark re-marks after a checkpoint
cases.note: A marks 100 and types statement 880. B, offline and not having seen A's mark, marks the same bill and period paid (+300s). B's deleted=false is the latest mark and is after the checkpoint, so the payment counts on top of the checkpoint that already includes it: 780, not 880. No per-field rule can tell this from a real re-mark; the user corrects it by typing Remaining (sync-protocol.md 5.4).

cases.name: known limitation: a device that missed the checkpoint unmarks an absorbed payment
cases.note: B saw A's mark but not A's statement 880, so to B the payment is after its checkpoint and unmark writes only deleted=true. Merged: the payment is gone but the checkpoint still includes it, so Remaining stays 880 instead of 980 (sync-protocol.md 5.4).

cases.name: an amount edit after the checkpoint does not move a pre-checkpoint payment
cases.note: Only the mark HLC is compared with the checkpoint.

cases.name: Remaining is clamped at zero
cases.note: 50 - 80 is shown as 0.

cases.name: migration stamp: payments at the checkpoint's own HLC are not subtracted
cases.note: The migration writes every row at one HLC. 'After the checkpoint' is strict, so existing payments already reflected in today's Remaining are not subtracted a second time.

cases.name: money is aggregated in integer cents
cases.note: Each amount is rounded to cents before summing: 10000 - 10 - 20 - 3334 = 6636 cents. 33.335 rounds to 33.34 under data-model.md section 3 (33.335 * 100 = 3333.5 in binary floating point).

cases.name: extra payments with random IDs add up
cases.note: Two devices each record an extra 100; both are separate payments.

cases.name: an unmarked extra payment does not count
cases.note: Deleting an extra payment works like unmark.

cases.name: set-asides never lower Remaining; balance sums set-asides with no regular payment yet
cases.note: Set-aside payments use their own deterministic ID and kind SetAside.

cases.name: set-aside balance restarts after a regular payment
cases.note: Only set-asides in periods after the latest live Regular payment's period count (P3 only). The regular payment lowers Remaining; set-asides never do.

cases.name: duplicate set-aside on two devices yields one row
cases.note: Like regular payments, set-asides are deterministic per (bill, period).

cases.name: a deleted bill has no Remaining; its payments stay as rows
cases.note: Payments are not cascaded; apps hide payments of deleted bills.

cases.name: restore re-stamps the backup and tombstones rows missing from it
cases.note: A restores at +1000s a backup with BILL_1 (Remaining 1145), its P1 payment and PayAnchor. BILL_2 is tombstoned. Synced settings missing from the backup are set to null (defaults); Notion connector settings, unknown setting keys, device rows and unknown entities are never touched. B's offline P2 payment (+900s, unknown to A) survives as a row but is before the restore checkpoint, so it does not lower Remaining; B's P3 payment after the restore does: 1145 - 60 = 1085.

cases.name: settings: last write wins per key, keys are independent
cases.note: Settings have no deleted field; a null value means 'use the default' (here: reset the Loans colour).

cases.name: the same paycheck recorded on two devices merges into one row
cases.note: Paycheck IDs are derived from (income source, pay date).

cases.name: unknown entities and fields from a newer app version are kept
cases.note: Older apps store and forward records they do not understand, and include them in snapshots.

cases.name: invalid records are ignored
cases.note: A record needs string entity, id, field and hlc (valid HLC), and a value that is null, boolean, number or string. Unknown extra keys are ignored. A missing value key is invalid; null must be explicit.

cases.name: payment kind: missing or wrong type reads as Regular, an unknown string does not count
cases.note: kind null, kind 5 and a missing kind are the default Regular (data-model.md 1.2) and count: 1200 - 10 - 20 - 80 = 1090. kind "Refund" is an unknown value and does not count.

cases.name: set-aside balance ignores payments whose periodKey is not a valid date
cases.note: Regular payments with an invalid periodKey do not reset the balance and set-asides with one are not counted. They still lower Remaining (Regular): 600 - 100 - 50 = 450.

cases.name: two payouts on one day from an Irregular source stay two rows
cases.note: Irregular actuals use random UUIDv7 IDs (like Extra payments); only scheduled cadences derive the ID from (source, pay date).

cases.name: echo: Notion reporting the value the connector last pushed creates no checkpoint
cases.note: A pushed Remaining=1000 to Notion, then read it back. B's offline payment (HLC +300s) is not yet on A. Treating the echo as an edit would set a checkpoint at +400s and silently drop B's payment.

cases.name: Notion edit with a new value creates a checkpoint
cases.note: The user typed a statement balance of 975 in Notion. It differs from the last pushed value, so it is a real edit: checkpoint 975 at A's next HLC. B's earlier payment (+300s) is treated as included.

cases.name: app edit to the current computed value creates no checkpoint
cases.note: On A, Remaining shows 900. Saving the editor with 900 unchanged must not write a checkpoint, or B's offline payment would be dropped.

cases.name: app edit to a new value creates a checkpoint; later payments still subtract
cases.note: A sets 880 at +400s. B's payment at +500s is after it: 880 - 50 = 830.

cases.name: Notion value equal to the current computed value creates no checkpoint
cases.note: Not an echo (last pushed was 1000), but unchanged from what A computes, so nothing is written.

cases.name: markPaid writes the deterministic payment with every mark field
cases.note: Fields written: amountPaid, billId, deleted=false, kind, paidAt, periodKey, all at the op's HLC.

cases.name: markPaid after unmark reuses the deterministic ID
cases.note: Re-marking writes deleted=false at a new HLC, which also becomes the payment's mark HLC.

cases.name: unmarkPaid tombstones the deterministic payment
cases.note: Unmark writes only deleted=true.

cases.name: unmarkPaid on a payment that is not live writes nothing
cases.note: Nothing to unmark.

cases.name: markPaid for a set-aside uses the set-aside ID and does not lower Remaining
cases.note: Kind SetAside.
